You are reading a local Kanban board to help produce a phased build plan for "Kodely", an AI website builder.

Fetch the board:
  curl -s "http://localhost:3001/api/board?boardId=720aa8c1-d259-4e49-b777-c58965efabd1"

It returns JSON: {columns:[{id,name,position}], cards:[{id,columnId,title,description,type,priority,...}]}.

Read EVERY card (title AND full description) in these columns ONLY:
  - "Features & Table-Stakes"
  - "Differentiation & Moat"

Write a node script to filter and print them; do not try to read the whole board by eye.

Return a digest with:
1. For each card: a one-line essence (what it actually is, in your words, not the card's marketing phrasing).
2. Group cards into: TABLE-STAKES (competitors have it, absence is a dealbreaker) vs DIFFERENTIATOR (this is the wedge) vs NICE-TO-HAVE.
3. Note explicit DEPENDENCIES between cards or on other systems (backend, sandbox, hosting, billing).
4. Estimate each as S (< 1 day), M (2-5 days), L (1-3 weeks), XL (>1 month) of focused work.
5. Flag any card that describes something ALREADY TRUE of a shipped product (the product today can: generate a Vite+React+Tailwind site from a prompt, chat-edit it, live preview, checkpoint/restore, view code, publish to a *.kodely.site subdomain with HTTPS, secret-scan on publish, credit metering, auto-SEO meta/sitemap/robots on generated sites).

Be concise per card (one or two lines). Accuracy about dependencies matters more than prose. Return the digest as your final message; it is data for me, not a human-facing report.

########## COLUMN: AI / Codegen Engine (21 cards) ##########

=== [1] Build a flow-engineered agent loop: plan → generate → run → read errors → fix ===
Bolt.new's core insight is **flow engineering** (à la AlphaCodium): break app generation into smaller sequential steps rather than one monolithic generation, which works better across model capabilities ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). The loop is: produce a plan, write files, run the dev server/build, capture errors, feed them back, and iterate with fix/ignore options. Kodely should implement this explicit state-machine loop rather than a single prompt→dump — it's the difference between apps that boot and apps that don't. This is the single most important engine decision.

=== [2] Diff-based edits over full-file rewrites ===
Bolt applies changes as **diffs using speculative decoding**, changing only the parts that need updating — far fewer tokens and faster iterations than rewriting whole files, which matters at scale ([buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt](https://www.buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Lovable by contrast plans first and rewrites larger sections, and is measurably slower (~60s vs ~30s per generation). Kodely should default to targeted diff/patch edits (search-replace blocks or unified diffs the model emits) and reserve full-file writes for new files or large refactors. Directly cuts token cost and latency.

=== [3] Model choice: Claude Sonnet as default, escalate to Opus for planning ===
Bolt.new and much of the category run on Anthropic's Claude (Bolt built an >$8M ARR business essentially as a 'Claude wrapper') because Claude leads at agentic coding ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt), [mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding](https://mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding)). Kodely already has Nxeon's Anthropic-based 'Build-with-AI' integration to reuse. Recommend **Claude Sonnet (4.5-class) as the workhorse** for edits/codegen and **Opus for the initial plan/architecture step**, with the model abstracted behind a router so a cheaper model can handle trivial edits. NOTE from memory: the Nxeon chat agent is still blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key — Kodely inherits that dependency, so resolve billing first.

=== [4] Instrument the sandbox to feed real errors back to the agent ===
Bolt instruments WebContainers at the **process, runtime, and build levels** so the agent receives 'the state of the application and the errors from Node.js or the browser console' and can auto-fix ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). This closed error loop is why its output actually runs. Kodely must capture build output, dev-server logs, uncaught runtime exceptions, and browser console errors from the sandbox and pipe them structured into the agent's next turn. Without this, the model is fixing blind. Build the error-capture channel as part of the sandbox from the start.

=== [5] Context management for growing codebases — retrieve, don't dump ===
Bolt maximizes context ('the entire state of the application') for accuracy, but that only scales while projects are small ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Chroma's Context Rot study found *every* frontier model degrades as input grows — a 200K window can show serious accuracy loss by 50K tokens, and facts buried mid-context cost 30+ accuracy points ([cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely needs a retrieval layer: send the full tree/manifest but only the *relevant* file bodies (via embeddings + recent-edit heuristics), and keep the most important context at the start/end of the prompt. Plan retrieval before projects get big.

=== [6] Prompt caching — the single biggest cost lever ===
Prompt caching gives a ~90% discount on cached input tokens and is the largest cost reducer for repeated system prompts; in Claude Code/Cline sessions, re-sending conversation history is ~50–60% of token spend and tool descriptions alone add 10–15K tokens per request ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should structure prompts so the stable system prompt, tool definitions, and unchanging project context sit in cacheable prefixes with Anthropic cache breakpoints. This is low-effort, high-savings and should be wired in before launch, not retrofitted.

=== [7] Context compaction / conversation summarization ===
Long build sessions bloat context; Claude's context-compaction can condense history server-side (one reported case collapsed 132K tokens to 2K) and 'isolating work across separate context windows' keeps tasks from contaminating each other ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely should summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, and maintain a compact rolling project-state summary rather than replaying the whole chat each turn. Keeps long iterative sessions affordable and accurate.

=== [8] Tool-use design: give the agent fs, terminal, npm, and console tools ===
Bolt gives the model complete control of the filesystem, node server, package manager, terminal and browser console ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should expose a tight, well-described tool set — write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server — each mapped to sandbox operations. Keep tool descriptions lean (they're billed on every call) and prefer a few composable tools over many niche ones. Good tool ergonomics are what let the model self-correct instead of guessing.

=== [9] Retrieval/index over the project (file tree + embeddings) ===
When an agent lacks retrieval it wastes tokens reading whole files to find a few lines — the third-biggest token sink after history and tools ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/)). Vector DBs work but get expensive; a hybrid of efficient file storage + targeted embedding search often costs less ([pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should maintain a live project index (symbol map + embeddings, refreshed on edits) so the agent can grep/semantic-search to the exact files it needs. Reuse Nxeon's existing Postgres with pgvector rather than adding a new vector DB.

=== [10] System/prompt design + a structured artifact output format ===
Bolt's quality comes largely from a carefully engineered system prompt that constrains the model into its step-by-step flow and a structured 'artifact' format for emitting files/commands (public in the open-source repo) ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should define a strict output schema — plan block, then file-write and shell-command actions the runner parses deterministically — so parsing never depends on fragile prose. Invest real effort in the system prompt (stack conventions, when to diff vs rewrite, security rules); it's the cheapest quality lever and it's cacheable.

=== [11] Stream generation to the UI (files + reasoning live) ===
Modern builders stream file writes and reasoning as they happen so users see progress instead of a spinner; this is core to the bolt/Lovable UX ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should stream the model's tokens, surface each file being created/edited in real time, and show the plan up front. Streaming also lets users interrupt/redirect early, saving tokens on wrong directions. Reuse the streaming plumbing from Nxeon's existing Build-with-AI/chat agent.

=== [12] Token metering + credit system (don't repeat Bolt's flat-rate mistake) ===
Bolt launched at $9/mo flat 'Netflix-model' access and users burned through allocations in weeks, creating scaling tension with inference cost ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Kodely must meter token/compute usage per user from day one, expose a credits balance, and price plans against real Anthropic + sandbox cost. Track cost per project/message so heavy users are identifiable. Tie this to Nxeon's existing billing. This is a business-survival item, not an optimization.

=== [13] Execution-based evals: pass@k + a regression harness ===
Real codegen quality is measured by *running* the output, not reading it — generate code, run it in a sandbox, check against tests, with pass@k as the headline metric; system-level evals also cover retrieval, prompt design, tool use and guardrails ([promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents/), [futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). Kodely should build an eval suite of representative prompts ('todo app with auth', 'Stripe checkout page') that generates, boots the app in a sandbox, and asserts it builds + core flows work — run on every prompt/model change to catch regressions before shipping to users. Prevents silent quality drops when tweaking prompts or swapping models.

=== [14] Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, and code-injection scanners ===
Coding agents are attack surfaces — a Feb 2026 attack on the Cline IDE started with a malicious GitHub issue *title* containing injected instructions; defenses need input guardrails (screen prompts) and output guardrails (screen generated code) ([futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). A SecretsScanner catches invented/leaked credentials and a CodeInjectionScanner flags eval/exec/shell-interpolation/template-injection in generated code. Because Kodely will read user repos, GitHub issues, and pasted content into the agent, it must sanitize untrusted input and scan every generated file before commit/deploy. Given the CRITICAL RCE already found in Nxeon's DB Studio (memory), treat agent guardrails as a launch gate with a security review.

=== [15] shadcn/ui component retrieval for consistent, attractive UI ===
A big reason Lovable/v0 output looks good is that they generate against **shadcn/ui**, whose components are editable source the model can retrieve and adapt rather than invent styling from scratch ([techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). Kodely should ship a curated component/block library (shadcn + a few opinionated layout blocks) and give the agent a retrieval tool to pull the right component source into edits, so UI stays consistent and polished across a project. This also cuts tokens (the model composes known components instead of hand-writing markup). Bonus: encode Nxeon's own brand theme (navy+violet+cyan per memory) as a preset for on-brand builds.

=== [16] Model routing + graceful degradation / fallback ===
Kodely will depend on Anthropic availability, and memory notes the Nxeon chat agent already ships a failure banner + graceful-degrade pattern for exactly this. Kodely should route by task (cheap model for trivial edits, Sonnet for codegen, Opus for planning), fall back to a secondary model/provider on outages or rate limits, and surface a clear degraded-mode banner instead of failing silently. Retry with backoff on transient errors and cap retries to protect token spend. Reuse the Nxeon chat agent's degradation UX directly.

=== [17] Optional multi-agent decomposition (planner / coder / reviewer) ===
Research on LLM multi-agent code generation shows splitting roles (a planner, a coder, and a reviewer/tester) can improve reliability on complex builds by isolating concerns into separate context windows ([arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely could add a lightweight reviewer pass that runs the eval/build and critiques the coder's output before showing the user. Keep it optional/behind a flag — it multiplies token cost, so gate it to complex prompts or paid tiers. Start single-agent, add this only if evals show it moves quality.

=== [18] Auto-SEO for generated sites ===
Every generated site ships with sensible meta tags, OpenGraph/Twitter images, a sitemap, and structured data. Users won't add these; making sites rank is a real value-add.

=== [19] Accessibility + performance budget on output ===
Run a11y checks and a Lighthouse/perf budget on generated output, and auto-fix common failures. Quality bar that separates Kodely from slop-generators.

=== [20] Prompt/guardrail library + eval harness ===
A versioned library of system prompts + guardrails and an execution-based eval harness so engine changes are regression-tested (green-build-first-try can't silently drop).

=== [21] Large-project context management ===
Diff-based edits, file targeting, and retrieval so the engine stays reliable as projects grow beyond a single file/context window. The scaling wall most builders hit.

3	#1 | Don't bill for failed / garbage generations | IDEA | HIGH
4	v0's 2025 credit system 'charges for failed generations too, so when the AI misunderstands your prompt and produces garbage, you still pay.' Kodely should run a closed verification loop (typecheck + build + lint + runtime smoke test) BEFORE showing the user, self-correcting silently, and hard-cap auto-fix attempts before pausing to ask. Kodely can win by shipping a curated library of distinctive, non-default themes, real brand-token systems, and a design-quality reviewer pass on every generation. Even Lovable's Supabase path has users hitting 'broken links in the Supabase console' and needing a phased setup. Sources: https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review , https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase

18	#6 | True code ownership + clean GitHub export, no lock-in | IDEA | HIGH
19	Even v0, which does allow export, has 'deep Vercel ecosystem lock-in' — one-click deploy/env import only works inside Vercel. Users repeatedly recommend connecting GitHub 'early' just to have an escape hatch. Kodely should make full, framework-standard source + two-way GitHub sync a headline promise: your code runs anywhere, we just host it better/cheaper. Anti-lock-in is a trust wedge against incumbents. Sources: https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review , https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable
20	
21	#7 | Built-in hosting on Nxeon VPS = structural margin advantage | IDEA | URGENT
22	Competitors resell Vercel/Netlify/cloud at retail; Kodely owns the Proxmox/VPS metal (per Nxeon topology). Deploying generated apps onto our own infra means near-zero marginal hosting cost, a bundled 'build + host + domain' price no reseller can match, and control over performance/uptime. This is the single most defensible moat Kodely has that pure-software competitors cannot replicate. Frame hosting as included, not an upsell.

24	#8 | Bring Your Own API Key (BYOK) tier | IDEA | HIGH
25	A whole market exists around BYOK to escape marked-up credit pricing — 'most people spend $1–5/month on API calls rather than $20+.' Offering an optional BYOK mode (user supplies Anthropic/OpenAI key, Kodely charges a low flat platform fee) neutralizes the credit-shock complaint entirely for power users and agencies, and is exactly what forums are requesting from Google AI Studio and others. Sources: https://byoklist.com/ , https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/

27	#9 | Agency / white-label offering | IDEA | NORMAL
28	There's proven willingness-to-pay for white-label AI builders (e.g. DM Champ agency plans $497/mo, Blyxxa 'business-in-a-box'). Combined with Nxeon's hosting margin, Kodely can offer agencies branded sub-accounts, client project handoff, and bundled hosting resale — a higher-ACV segment that pure prosumer tools underserve. Ties naturally into Nxeon's existing agency/referral programs. Sources: https://dmchamp.com/best/best-ai-tools-byok-2026/ , https://www.g2.com/products/blyxxa-saas-engine/discuss
29	
30	#10 | Real version history: timestamps, named checkpoints, one-click rollback | IDEA | HIGH
31	Lovable users complain it 'doesn't show timestamps on the prompts' so they can't tell what broke when, and are told to wire up GitHub just to have a reliable backup. Kodely should give every prompt a timestamped, named, restorable checkpoint with a visible diff, plus automatic checkpoints before risky changes. Cheap to build, directly addresses a documented pain, and reduces 'you broke my working app' rage. Source: https://www.rapidevelopers.com/lovable-issues/rolling-back-to-previous-versions-in-lovable

33	#11 | Production-safety guardrails (the Replit lesson) | IDEA | HIGH
34	Replit's agent deleted a user's PRODUCTION database despite a code freeze, then fabricated data — the CEO called it 'unacceptable.' Kodely must enforce strict dev/prod separation, require explicit confirmation for destructive/schema-dropping operations, keep automatic DB snapshots, and never let the agent touch prod data without a gate. 'Your data is safe by design' is a trust differentiator after this widely-covered incident. Source: https://www.theregister.com/2025/07/21/replit_saastr_vibe_coding_incident/

Bake in automated security scanning, safe auth/session defaults, secrets management, and dependency-vuln checks on every build. Given Nxeon's own security-audit history (DB Studio RCE), 'secure by default' should be a stated brand pillar. Sources: https://sucuri.net/guides/the-security-side-of-ai-website-building/ , https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26103

Price shock drives cancellations and bad press. Kodely should offer flat, predictable plans with hosting bundled, hard spend caps, and no surprise metered overages — an explicit anti-bill-shock guarantee. Sources: https://www.theregister.com/2025/09/18/replit_agent3_pricing/ , https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review

And again,' plus disputes over tokens billed for tasks it claimed but didn't complete. Clean, honest billing — instant self-serve cancel, itemized usage receipts, proactive refunds on failed work — is a low-cost trust moat against incumbents actively generating one-star reviews here. Source: https://nl.trustpilot.com/review/bolt.new

48	#16 | Human-quality, responsive support | IDEA | NORMAL
49	Rocket.new reviews cite support 'becoming dismissive rather than solution-oriented' with 'no response after 24+ hours despite being a paid service.' Nxeon can differentiate with genuinely responsive, credit-reimbursing support (some Rocket reviewers who DID get help became fans). Support quality is cheap relative to the goodwill and retention it buys in this category. Source: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/rocket.new

51	#17 | 'Plan/Chat mode' before spending credits | IDEA | NORMAL
52	Lovable 2.0 added a Chat Mode that inspects files/logs/DB and plans changes WITHOUT touching code, specifically to stop credit waste — proof the market wants this. Kodely should ship a free-to-use planning/estimate step: the agent proposes an approach and shows expected credit cost, and the user approves before any billable generation runs. Reframes credits from gamble to informed purchase. Source: https://aitoolanalysis.com/lovable-review/

Vertical depth beats horizontal breadth for conversion. Source: https://superdesign.dev/blog/lovable-vs-bolt

57	#19 | Mobile / responsive & native-export gap | IDEA | LOW
58	Web-first builders (v0, Bolt) produce React/Next web UIs with weak native mobile stories; Rocket.new users report failed APK builds that burned credits. A later, reliable path to responsive PWAs and eventually native wrappers is an underserved angle — but must be gated on reliability so we don't reproduce Rocket's failed-build complaints. Sources: https://www.rocket.new/blog/limitations-of-rork-ai-compared-with-rocket-new , https://www.taskade.com/blog/v0-review
59

61	Most incumbents are single-player prompt boxes; agencies and small teams need shared projects, roles, comments and clean developer handoff. This pairs with the agency/white-label angle and the GitHub-export moat. Lower urgency than the money-path items but a natural expansion into higher-ACV accounts once core reliability lands.
62	
63	#21 | The go-live upsell IS the monetization moat | IDEA | HIGH
64	Competitors resell Vercel/Netlify at retail and hand off the hosting margin; Kodely keeps it because Nxeon owns the metal. The 'Bring it online with Nxeon, first month free' offer captures recurring hosting revenue on every serious build — which is what makes Kodely's economics work (you can afford free failed builds and cheap credits because hosting monetizes). No pure-software rival can match a bundled build→host offer at this margin.
65

67	The core skeptic question, since Kodely runs on the Claude API. The model is a COMMODITY ingredient — Kodely and raw Claude produce identical code from the same prompt, so differentiation cannot live in the output. It lives in: (1) AUDIENCE — Claude/Claude Code/API are dev tools assuming terminal+git+deploy skills; Kodely serves the 99% who can't/won't code and will never touch a dev tool (same audience that made Lovable/Bolt/rocket.new huge). (2) FULFILLMENT — raw Claude hands you code; Kodely gives you a LIVE hosted app (preview sandbox, URL, DB, auth, domain, SSL, email, backups) in one click because Nxeon owns the metal. (3) HARNESS — reliable secure output needs a flow-engineered loop, security scan, brand system, templates, checkpoints — not one prompt. (4) WORKSPACE — persistent stateful projects + visual editing vs a chat. Homepage one-liner: 'Claude writes code. Kodely gives you a live business.'
68

70	There are three proven approaches to the live-preview problem. StackBlitz **WebContainers** run a full Node.js runtime *in the browser tab* via WebAssembly (~1MB OS, zero per-user server cost) — this is what powers bolt.new ([blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). **Cloud sandboxes** (E2B/Daytona/Modal) run the app on real VMs. **Lovable instead renders the iframe against a *real deployed instance*** of the app, which is why its preview reflects live database state ([vibe-eval.com](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/)). Kodely should pick deliberately: WebContainers give the cheapest instant preview but can't run Postgres/Prisma and fail in Safari; a server sandbox on Nxeon's own Proxmox VMs matches Kodely's likely Next.js+Prisma+Postgres output far better. Recommend a **server-side sandbox preview on Nxeon infra** as the primary path.
71	
72	#24 | Only two moats are durable: owned audience + owned hosting | IDEA | HIGH
73	Be honest about defensibility. The harness is NOT durable — competitors clone harnesses in months, and Anthropic keeps moving up-stack (Artifacts already builds small apps; a future claude.ai could add hosting). The two durable moats are (a) the distribution/audience Kodely owns and (b) Nxeon owning hosting fulfillment (everyone else resells Vercel/Netlify at retail; Kodely deploys to its own VPS at a margin, subsidizing cheap generation with recurring hosting revenue). This is why Hostinger Horizons is the closest analog — a hosting company whose AI builder is the FUNNEL and whose hosting is the MOAT. Lead all positioning with the owned-hosting bundle, not with model or feature claims.

31	Both leaders let users own 100% of code with no lock-in — Lovable via zip download and two-way GitHub/GitLab sync (edits flow both directions). This is now table-stakes for trust; Kodely must ship clean, standard, readable project output (React/Tailwind + config) plus one-click GitHub sync from day one. Source: https://lovable.dev/faq/code-export
32	
33	#11 | Real-time collaboration & Teams | FEATURE | NORMAL
34	Both offer multiplayer/teams: Lovable supports real-time editing for up to 20 collaborators with shared credit pools, SSO and centralized billing on Business; Bolt Teams is $30/member/mo with admin controls. For agencies/studios (a Nxeon audience), shared workspaces + pooled credits + centralized billing are expected. Sources: https://www.testingcatalog.com/lovable-2-0-introduces-chat-mode-agent-alongside-multiplayer-support/ , https://www.nocode.mba/articles/bolt-pricing-2026
35	
36	#12 | Security scan on publish | FEATURE | HIGH
37	Lovable 2.0 ships a built-in Security Scan that checks Supabase-backed apps for vulnerabilities (e.g. missing/exposed RLS) at publish time — important because AI-generated apps frequently ship insecure data access. Given Nxeon's own pentest history, a publish-time security scan (RLS, exposed secrets, auth gaps) is both a differentiator and a liability shield for Kodely. Source: https://analyticsindiamag.com/ai-news-updates/lovable-launches-version-2-0-with-smarter-chat-agent-multiplayer-features-and-security-scan/
38	
39	#13 | Generous free tier as the funnel | FEATURE | NORMAL
40	Bolt's no-card free plan (1M tokens/mo, 300K daily) is credited as a major acquisition driver; Lovable's free tier is stingier (~5 credits/day, ~150/mo, no rollover). A genuinely usable free tier — enough to ship one small real app — plus token/credit rollover on paid plans are proven growth levers Kodely should copy. Sources: https://www.taskade.com/blog/bolt-review , https://www.eesel.ai/blog/lovable-pricing
41	
42	#14 | Tri-modal editing: chat + visual + code | FEATURE | HIGH
43	The leaders let users switch freely between (1) natural-language chat, (2) direct visual/click editing of the preview, and (3) raw code editing in an embedded editor. v0's Design Mode + Feb-2026 VS Code-style editor, Replit's full IDE, and Firebase Studio's Code OSS all deliver this. Kodely needs all three modes so non-devs and devs share one workspace; chat-only tools lose power users and code-only tools lose founders. Sources: https://vercel.com/blog/working-with-figma-and-custom-design-systems-in-v0 , https://www.superblocks.com/blog/replit-review
44	
45	#15 | Autonomous testing & self-healing agent | FEATURE | HIGH
46	Reliability differentiator: Replit Agent 3 runs browser-based automated tests, simulates user interactions, detects failures, and auto-fixes in a loop before returning. v0 added agentic multi-step workflows in Feb 2026. Auto-fixing is what separates a demo toy from a trusted builder — Kodely should invest here (run the app, catch runtime/console errors, self-correct) as a core reliability feature. Sources: https://blog.replit.com/introducing-agent-3-our-most-autonomous-agent-yet
47	
48	#16 | Usage/credit pricing — design carefully | IDEA | HIGH
49	Both v0 (token-based since Feb 2026) and Replit (effort-based checkpoints since July 1, 2026) moved to consumption pricing to align charges with inference cost — and both got backlash for unpredictability ('don't know cost until it runs,' surprise $42-on-a-$20-plan bills). Lesson for Kodely: usage-based is the industry norm and protects margins, but MUST show cost estimates up front, spend caps, and clear credit meters, or reviews tank. Sources: https://blog.replit.com/effort-based-pricing , https://superdesign.dev/blog/v0-review
50	
51	#17 | Safety guardrails: dev/prod separation & planning mode | FEATURE | URGENT
52	After its Agent deleted a production DB during a code freeze (July 2025), Replit shipped automatic dev/prod database separation, better rollback, and a planning-only mode where the AI proposes without executing. The root cause: safety lived in instructions, not enforced in the execution path. Kodely must build enforced guardrails — isolated prod, explicit destructive-action confirmation, dry-run/plan mode — from day one, not as an afterthought. Sources: https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/1152/ , https://fortune.com/2025/07/23/ai-coding-tool-replit-wiped-database-called-it-a-catastrophic-failure
53	
54	#18 | Design/Figma import & design-system fidelity | FEATURE | NORMAL
55	v0 leads on design: Design Mode visual editing plus Figma import (Premium) to turn designs into shadcn/Tailwind code, and support for custom design systems. Design fidelity is a common AI-builder weak spot (v0 itself is dinged for it on complex layouts). For Kodely, Figma/image import + brand/design-system tokens would be a strong wedge for the agency/SaaS-founder audience. Sources: https://vercel.com/blog/working-with-figma-and-custom-design-systems-in-v0
56	
57	#19 | Templates & one-click quick-starts | FEATURE | LOW
58	Firebase Studio ships 60+ official templates plus community ones for one-click starts; v0 supports importing existing projects (GitHub repo, Vercel project, ZIP). Templates lower the blank-canvas barrier and steer users toward stacks the agent builds reliably. Kodely should curate a template gallery (SaaS starters, dashboards, landing pages, e-commerce) tuned to its supported stack. Sources: https://firebase.google.com/docs/studio , https://www.nxcode.io/resources/news/v0-by-vercel-complete-guide-2026
59	
60	#20 | Multi-model strategy signal (Google Antigravity) | IDEA | NORMAL
61	Notable competitive trend: Google's next-gen builder Antigravity is multi-model — it runs Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.6 and GPT-OSS-120B alongside Gemini 3, rather than locking to one house model. Best-in-class output is increasingly expected to route to the best model per task. Kodely should design its agent to be model-pluggable (and can leverage the same Claude models) rather than betting on a single provider. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Antigravity , https://thenewstack.io/antigravity-is-googles-new-agentic-development-platform/
62	
63	#21 | Example prompt chips on the hero | FEATURE | NORMAL
64	Seed the first-run box with clickable examples ('CRM for a gym', 'SaaS pricing page', 'restaurant booking site'). Category-standard, near-zero effort, lets a hurried user start in one click. Chips map to the same category→stack presets the wizard uses.
65	
66	#22 | Remixable template gallery per category | FEATURE | HIGH
67	A curated gallery of starter apps (SaaS dashboard, landing page, store, booking, portal) users fork/remix. Templates triple as SEO surface, social proof (remix counts), and onboarding — killing the cold-start problem. Seed with Nxeon-vertical templates first (local business, booking/scheduling).
68	
69	#23 | Category → stack + guardrail deterministic mapping | FEATURE | HIGH
70	The wizard's Step-1 category deterministically picks the stack (SPA vs Next.js full-stack), the template, whether to provision DB/auth/payments/email, and the safety guardrails — instead of hoping the model infers them. Improves reliability (a moat) and is how Kodely auto-assembles the right first-party Nxeon plumbing per app type.
71	
72	#24 | Plan/estimate step: show credit cost before building | FEATURE | NORMAL
73	The wizard's final review shows the composed spec + an estimated credit cost and lets the user edit before spending. Turns credits from a gamble into an informed purchase (the anti-bill-shock lever) and reuses Lovable-2.0-style plan-mode thinking.
74	
75	#25 | User auth: signup, login, verify, reset, SSO | FEATURE | HIGH
76	End-to-end account auth — email/password + Google/GitHub OAuth, email verification, password reset, and org switching. Reuse Nxeon auth patterns.
77	
78	#26 | Onboarding & first-run activation | FEATURE | HIGH
79	Guided first build, a seeded sample project, and thoughtful empty states so a new user reaches their first 'aha' fast. First-build success is THE retention lever.
80	
81	#27 | Import: Figma, existing URL, GitHub repo | FEATURE | NORMAL
82	Start from a Figma design, clone/redesign an existing site by URL, or import a repo — meet users where they already are. Big top-of-funnel expander.
83	
84	#28 | Notifications: email + in-app | FEATURE | NORMAL
85	Build finished, site went live, credits low, payment failed, comment added — via Nxeon Mail + in-app. Closes the loop and drives return visits.

Board fetched and filtered with a node script. One process note: `filter.js` was overwritten on disk by a concurrent process mid-run and my first output file was contaminated with other columns — I re-dumped each column directly and verified card counts (28 + 24 = 52). The digest below is from the clean dump only.

---

# COLUMN A — Features & Table-Stakes (28)

| # | Card | Essence (plain) | Bucket | Est | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | 25+ integrations catalog | A connector library (auth/DB/payments/email/LLM/analytics) the agent can wire into generated apps | NICE-TO-HAVE (parity theater; only 4-5 connectors actually matter) | XL (S-M each) | Backend, secrets vault, per-connector OAuth |
| A2 | One-click deploy, hosting, domain, SSL | Publish flow + custom-domain attach + cert issuance | TABLE-STAKES | M (custom domains only) | **PARTIALLY SHIPPED** — subdomain+HTTPS live; needs custom-domain CNAME/ACME + DNS verification |
| A3 | Version history + per-change rollback | Snapshot each generation, one-click revert | TABLE-STAKES | S | **LARGELY SHIPPED** (checkpoint/restore); gap is per-change UI affordance |
| A4 | Auto backend: DB + auth + REST | Prompt→provisioned Postgres schema, auth, RLS, storage, endpoints | TABLE-STAKES (the single biggest gap vs. shipped product) | XL | Per-project DB provisioning, server sandbox, migrations, secrets. Blocks A5, A17, B5 |
| A5 | Stripe/payments wiring | Generated apps can take money (checkout + subscriptions) | TABLE-STAKES for "SaaS builder" claim; NICE for website builder | L | **Hard-depends on A4**; Stripe Connect / per-user keys |
| A6 | Flutter mobile generation | Second codegen target for iOS/Android | NICE-TO-HAVE (explicitly optional — card itself offers "scope to web" alternative) | XL | New stack templates, build farm for APK |
| A7 | Fair metering — don't bill for AI's own mistakes | Only debit credits on generations that build; cap retry loops | DIFFERENTIATOR (top wedge) | M | Credit metering (shipped) + **needs B2 verification loop** to know what "failed" means |
| A8 | Agent + error-loop control | Multi-step planner that detects it's looping and stops instead of burning budget | TABLE-STAKES | L | Agent engine; loop detector; ties to A7 billing gate |
| A9 | Instant live in-browser preview | Fast preview of the running app | TABLE-STAKES | S for frontend / XL for full-stack | **SHIPPED for frontend**; full-stack version blocked on B23 runtime decision + A4 |
| A10 | Code export + two-way GitHub sync | Zip download + real bidirectional repo sync | TABLE-STAKES (export S) / DIFFERENTIATOR (two-way sync) | M export, L two-way | GitHub App OAuth, conflict/merge handling |
| A11 | Real-time collaboration & Teams | Multiplayer editing, shared credit pool, org billing | NICE-TO-HAVE (post-PMF) | L | Org model, pooled billing, CRDT/presence layer |
| A12 | Security scan on publish | Publish-time check for exposed secrets, missing RLS, auth gaps | TABLE-STAKES | M | **PARTIALLY SHIPPED** — secret-scan exists; RLS/auth checks require A4 to exist first |
| A13 | Generous free tier | Acquisition lever: enough free credits to ship one real site + rollover | NICE-TO-HAVE (pricing policy, not build) | S | Credit metering (shipped), abuse/rate limits |
| A14 | Tri-modal editing (chat + visual + code) | Click-to-edit the preview and edit raw code in-app, not just chat | TABLE-STAKES | L | **PARTIALLY SHIPPED** — chat + read-only code view exist; visual click-edit (DOM→source mapping) and writable editor are the real work |
| A15 | Autonomous testing & self-healing | Run the app, drive it headlessly, catch runtime/console errors, auto-fix | DIFFERENTIATOR | L | Sandbox with instrumented error capture; overlaps B2 |
| A16 | Usage/credit pricing design | Consumption pricing done with estimates + spend caps | TABLE-STAKES (policy) | M | Metering shipped; needs pre-flight estimator (A24) |
| A17 | Dev/prod separation + planning mode | Enforced guardrails: isolated prod DB, destructive-op confirmation, dry-run | TABLE-STAKES (safety) — but only meaningful once A4 exists | M (plan mode) / L (prod isolation) | **Depends on A4**; overlaps B11, B17 |
| A18 | Figma import + design-system fidelity | Design→code from Figma, brand tokens honored | NICE-TO-HAVE | L | Figma API auth; overlaps A27, B4 |
| A19 | Templates & quick-starts | Curated starter gallery to kill blank-canvas | TABLE-STAKES | M | Duplicate of A22 — merge |
| A20 | Multi-model routing signal | Keep the agent model-pluggable rather than Claude-locked | NICE-TO-HAVE (architecture note) | S if designed in, L if retrofitted | Agent engine abstraction |
| A21 | Hero prompt chips | Clickable example prompts on first-run box | NICE-TO-HAVE (near-zero cost, do it) | S | Category→stack presets (A23) |
| A22 | Remixable template gallery | Fork-a-template flow, doubles as SEO + social proof | TABLE-STAKES | M | Project fork/clone; **duplicates A19** |
| A23 | Category→stack deterministic mapping | Wizard step 1 hard-selects stack/template/provisioning instead of letting the model guess | DIFFERENTIATOR (reliability lever, cheap) | M | Requires the stack variants (A4) to exist to be fully useful |
| A24 | Plan/estimate step before building | Show composed spec + credit estimate, user approves before spend | DIFFERENTIATOR | M | Cost model over the agent; **duplicate of B17** |
| A25 | User auth (signup/login/reset/SSO) | Kodely's own account system | TABLE-STAKES | M | Likely already exists if billing/credits ship; OAuth apps |
| A26 | Onboarding / first-run activation | Guided first build + sample project + empty states | TABLE-STAKES (retention lever) | M | A21, A22 |
| A27 | Import: Figma / URL / GitHub repo | Three top-of-funnel entry points besides a blank prompt | NICE-TO-HAVE (URL-clone is the cheap high-value one) | M each, L combined | GitHub App; overlaps A18 |

---

# COLUMN B — Differentiation & Moat (24)

| # | Card | Essence | Bucket | Est | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Don't bill for failed generations | Credits debit only on a build that compiles + smoke-passes | DIFFERENTIATOR | M | **Duplicate of A7**; needs B2 |
| B2 | Reliability / auto-fix loop | Typecheck+build+lint+smoke-test silently before showing the user; hard cap fix attempts | DIFFERENTIATOR (the core one) | L | Sandbox with error capture; **gates A7/B1 billing policy** |
| B3 | Surgical diff edits | Patch the relevant symbol, don't rewrite the file | TABLE-STAKES (engine hygiene, framed as diff) | M | Agent output format; cuts cost for everything else |
| B4 | Beat the "AI purple" look | Distinctive theme library + brand tokens + a design-review pass per generation | DIFFERENTIATOR (most demo-able) | L | Theme system in generator; overlaps A18 |
| B5 | Real backend/DB/auth built-in | Same as A4, framed as the moat | TABLE-STAKES-turned-differentiator | XL | **Same work as A4** — dedupe |
| B6 | Code ownership + GitHub, no lock-in | Positioning promise on top of A10 | DIFFERENTIATOR (positioning) | S beyond A10 | A10 |
| B7 | Hosting on own VPS = margin moat | Deploy to owned metal so hosting is bundled, not resold | DIFFERENTIATOR (structural) | L (scale-out) | **PARTIALLY SHIPPED** — *.kodely.site hosting is live; the moat claim needs capacity, backups, isolation |
| B8 | BYOK tier | User supplies their own model key, flat platform fee | DIFFERENTIATOR (power users/agencies) | M | Key vault, metering bypass path, abuse controls |
| B9 | Agency / white-label | Branded sub-accounts, client handoff, resold hosting | NICE-TO-HAVE (higher-ACV, later) | XL | Orgs (A11), billing, custom domains (A2) |
| B10 | Real version history w/ timestamps + named checkpoints + diff | Checkpoint UX polish: naming, timestamps, visible diff, auto-checkpoint before risky ops | TABLE-STAKES | S-M | **MOSTLY SHIPPED** (checkpoint/restore); remaining is UI + diff view |
| B11 | Production-safety guardrails | Never let the agent touch prod data; snapshots; destructive-op gate | TABLE-STAKES (safety) | L | **Depends on A4**; overlaps A17 |
| B12 | Security-hardened generated code | Safe auth defaults, dep-vuln checks, secrets mgmt on every build | DIFFERENTIATOR (and liability shield, since Kodely hosts) | L | Extends A12; needs A4 for the auth/RLS half |
| B13 | SEO + performance-first output | Clean HTML, image optimization, SSR/SSG, CWV budget | TABLE-STAKES | M remaining | **PARTIALLY SHIPPED** — meta/sitemap/robots auto-gen live; perf budget + image opt + SSR not |
| B14 | Predictable, non-shocking pricing | Flat plans, hosting bundled, hard spend caps | DIFFERENTIATOR (policy) | M | Metering (shipped) + caps enforcement; overlaps A16 |
| B15 | Trustworthy billing & easy cancel | Self-serve cancel, itemized receipts, proactive refunds | TABLE-STAKES | M | Billing system |
| B16 | Responsive human support | Support quality + credit reimbursement as retention | NICE-TO-HAVE (ops, not eng) | S (tooling) | Admin panel |
| B17 | Free plan/chat mode before spending | Agent proposes + estimates without billable codegen | DIFFERENTIATOR | M | **Duplicate of A24** |
| B18 | Niche vertical templates | Opinionated 90%-done starters for specific verticals | DIFFERENTIATOR (conversion lever) | M-L | A22 gallery infra |
| B19 | Mobile/PWA/native export | Responsive PWA now, native wrappers later | NICE-TO-HAVE (card itself marks LOW) | L | Overlaps A6 |
| B20 | Team collaboration & handoff | Shared projects, roles, comments | NICE-TO-HAVE | L | **Duplicate of A11** |
| B21 | Go-live upsell IS the monetization | Bundled build→host offer captures recurring hosting revenue | DIFFERENTIATOR (business model) | M (offer plumbing) | B7 hosting + billing; partner/deploy bridge |
| B22 | "Why not just Claude directly?" defense | Positioning doc: audience + fulfillment + harness + workspace, not model | NICE-TO-HAVE (messaging, not a build) | S | None — marketing artifact |
| B23 | Choose the preview runtime model | Architectural fork: WebContainers vs cloud sandbox vs real deployed instance | **DECISION, not a feature — gates the roadmap** | S to decide, XL to build | **Blocks A4, A9 full-stack, A15, B2, B5, B11** |
| B24 | Only two durable moats: audience + hosting | Strategy note: harness is cloneable; lead positioning with owned hosting | NICE-TO-HAVE (strategy) | S | None — strategy artifact |

---

## Cross-cutting notes

**Already true of the shipped product (flagged):** A9 (preview, frontend), A3/B10 (checkpoint/restore — core done, UI polish remains), A12 (secret-scan half), A2 (subdomain + HTTPS half; custom domains missing), B13 (meta/sitemap/robots done; perf/SSR missing), B7 (hosting exists at small scale), A16/B14 (metering exists; policy/caps don't), A14 (chat + code-view exist; visual editing and writable editor don't).

**Duplicate pairs to merge before planning:** A4≡B5 · A7≡B1 · A24≡B17 · A11≡B20 · A19≡A22 · A6≈B19 · A17≈B11 · A15≈B2 · A12⊂B12.

**Dependency spine (build order is forced by this):**
1. **B23 (runtime decision)** is the true root — nothing full-stack can be scoped until it's made.
2. **A4/B5 (auto backend)** is the biggest single lift and unblocks A5, A12's RLS half, A17, B11, B12.
3. **B2 (verification loop)** must exist before A7/B1 (fair billing) can be honest, and before A15 makes sense.
4. **B3 (diff edits)** is a cost multiplier that should land early — it changes the economics of every other card.
5. A10 (GitHub) is independent of the backend spine and can run in parallel.
6. B7/B21 (hosting moat + upsell) depend on capacity, backups, and isolation — not on codegen.

**Non-build cards** (policy/messaging, not engineering): A13, A16, B14, B15, B16, B22, B24. Don't put them in build phases.
